metadata.title: The ’picking the fittest’ approach and spatial dynamics in China’s artificial intelligence regional development

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study uses a panel of 30 Chinese provincial-level regions (2006–2021) and estimates fixed-effects and spatial econometric models; it does not use student-level ILSA microdata. As a result, there are no sampling/replicate weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT, BRR) to apply, and the concept of survey-weighted estimation is not part of the analysis. The authors instead rely on region and time fixed effects to account for unobserved time-invariant regional heterogeneity and common shocks across years. The analytic sample is defined by data availability for the 30 provinces (excluding Tibet) and by constructing lagged variables and spatial weights from provincial capital coordinates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PVs) are not applicable because the dependent variable is regional AI patenting performance (patents per million population) derived from patent databases, not cognitive achievement scores from an ILSA assessment. The paper also does not describe any missing-data imputation or deletion rule for the constructed panel variables (e.g., RTA ICT, AIpat/Pop, controls), so the missing-data strategy is a reporting gap rather than a design feature.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The empirical dataset covers 30 Chinese provincial-level regions observed over 2006–2021; the starting year is selected due to the introduction of the 2006 Plan. Provincial-level regions comprise 22 provinces, 4 municipalities, and 4 autonomous regions; Tibet is excluded due to lack of data. The dependent variable is constructed from invention patents applied to CNIPA using a keyword/IPC/CPC search strategy, excluding design patents and utility models, and fractional counts are used when applicants span multiple regions. Key regressors (e.g., RTA ICT) are computed from ICT-related patents and standardized, then smoothed using a three-year moving average; all independent variables are lagged one year in the main panel specification.

main_findings.dataset_used: China provincial-level panel (2006–2021) — AI patenting performance (CNIPA) and ICT specialization (CNIPA patents)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Fixed-effects panel (OLS) and 2SLS: RTA ICT coefficient (AI zones) β=0.3302 (p<0.01); RTA ICT coefficient (no AI zones) β=0.2059 (p>0.1). 2SLS second stage: RTA ICT (AI zones) β=0.6705 (p<0.01) and RTA ICT (no AI zones) β=0.4984 (p<0.01). First-stage IV relevance: IV RTA ICT coefficient β=0.4535 (p<0.01) in the second stage of the first-stage equation; OLS baseline RTA ICT β=0.2964 (p<0.05).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using China provincial-level panel data (2006–2021) on AI patenting performance and ICT specialization, the study leveraged ICT specialization (RTA ICT), AI zone status, and regional control variables to estimate how specialization relates to AI patenting, finding that RTA ICT is positively associated with AIpat/Pop and that the effect is stronger in AI zone candidate regions after 2SLS correction for endogeneity. This indicates that strengthening ICT specialization in regions selected for AI zones can raise AI patenting output, but policy should also anticipate widening disparities between leading and lagging regions.

main_findings.dataset_used: China provincial-level panel (2006–2021) — spatial econometric SAR with control-function endogeneity correction
main_findings.target_variable: AI patenting performance spatial spillovers (neighboring AIpat/Pop)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Spatial Autoregressive (SAR) model: spatial lag of AI patenting performance WY coefficient β=−0.2162 (p<0.05). Control-function SAR second step: spatial lag WY coefficient β=−0.2064 (p<0.05) and RTA ICT coefficient β=0.3213 (p<0.05). Control-function residuals are significant: residuals for spatial lag νspatial lag β=0.0808 (p<0.05) and residuals for RTA ICT νRTA ICT β=0.8821 (p<0.1). Model fit comparison: SAR outperforms SDM by AIC/BIC (Table 2).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using China provincial-level panel data (2006–2021) with a spatial autoregressive diffusion structure and a control-function approach, the study leveraged neighboring AI patenting performance (spatial lag) and ICT specialization to estimate inter-regional spillovers, finding that higher AI patenting in neighboring regions is associated with lower AI patenting in the focal region (negative spatial spillovers). This indicates that proximity to AI-leading regions can impede AI patenting progress elsewhere, implying that regional AI policy should pair specialization with mechanisms that reduce competitive crowding-out and enable productive cross-regional collaboration.

data.outcome_summary: The paper analyzes a panel of 30 Chinese provincial-level regions from 2006–2021, using AI patenting performance (AI-related invention patents per million population from CNIPA) as the outcome and ICT specialization (RTA ICT based on ICT-related patent shares, standardized and smoothed with a three-year moving average) as the key explanatory variable. In fixed-effects and 2SLS specifications, ICT specialization is positively and significantly associated with AI patenting, with larger effects in candidate AI development zone regions (2SLS: RTA ICT β=0.6705 for AI zones; β=0.4984 for non-AI zones, both p<0.01). Spatial econometric results show negative inter-regional spillovers: the SAR spatial lag coefficient is β=−0.2162 (p<0.05) and remains negative in the control-function SAR (β=−0.2064, p<0.05). The study does not use ML algorithms or PVs, and it does not report a missing-data handling strategy, so transparency on data completeness is limited.
